jobs.title: Robotics Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Who We Are:**

Aurelius Systems is a VC backed defense tech startup building autonomous, edge deployed directed energy systems for counter-UAS. We build laser weapons to shoot down drones.

We're a small team of engineers, former US military operators, and subject matter experts scaling America's directed energy dominance. The first cost effective, reliable and robust laser weapon system.

Our namesake isn't an accident. Marcus Aurelius wrote about doing the work in front of you, every day, without excuses. Henry Ford didn't wait for permission to reinvent manufacturing. That's how we operate, small team, unreasonable output, no hiding behind the unachievable.

In addition to our San Francisco lab, we opened our Detroit manufacturing hub and field test weekly on our own 400-acre private range.

**The Role and Your Impact:**  
We need a Robotics Software Engineer who writes fast, correct C++ that runs on real hardware. You’ll work on the Archimedes stack alongside our Lead Software Engineer, taking raw sensor data and turning it into tracking, control and autonomy that has to work in real time. Performance and accuracy matter more than anything. Your scope grows as fast as you do; our Lead went from Founding Robotics Engineer to Lead in 12 months.

**What You’ll Own:**

* Production C++ across the stack: sensor ingestion, tracking, control and autonomy
* Working directly with drivers and raw sensor data, not pre-packaged inputs
* Threading, process architecture and performance on the paths you own
* Timing and latency analysis, and making the fixes it points to
* Python tooling for testing, analysis and the range
* Debugging on hardware at weekly field tests

**What We’re Looking For:**

* 2+ years writing production C++ that runs on real hardware or real-time systems
* Comfort below the abstraction layer: threading, concurrency, memory, performance profiling
* You implement, not just design. You’ve shipped code you wrote
* Evidence you learn fast: you got effective in a new domain in months, not years

**Where you probably come from:** We’re domain agnostic. Robotics, AV, drones, aerospace, F1 or automotive, maritime, embedded systems, compilers, or low-level C++ game engine and 3D simulation work all fit. A robotics degree isn’t required; the robotics is learnable on the job.

**We want to talk if:** You’ve written C++ where latency or timing actually mattered and you measured it. Bonus if your projects touch motion planning, dynamics, trajectory optimization, or state estimation.

**Not a fit if:** You’re web, backend or full stack; your C++ is light and your real work is in Python; you’ve never had a full-time role; or you design systems but don’t implement them.

**Nice to Haves:**

* ROS2 (a good signal, though we've moved past it)
* Rust or other systems languages
* Sensor integration and calibration
* Real-time Linux

**Education:** BS, MS or PhD in CS, EE, Robotics or equivalent. Track record matters more than degree.

**How You Operate:**

* Extreme bias for action. You'd rather build a prototype tomorrow than model it for a month
* You characterize your own systems before the field does
* Comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration in a startup environment
* You debug from first principles, not intuition alone
* Clear communicator across mechanical, electrical, optical, and software teams
* Self directed. You identify what needs to happen next and do it without being told

**Why Join Aurelius Systems:**

* Build more in 1 month than most engineers build in 1 year. We field test weekly. Your work goes downrange, not into a filing cabinet.
* Career velocity is real. With no middle management, there are no layers between you and impact.
* Work on a problem that actually matters. Small cheap drones are changing warfare. Our laser systems are the asymmetric answer — infinite magazine, near zero cost per shot, scalable to every base, border, facility, and truck.
* Join the densest defense startup ecosystem in the country. California is where the next generation of defense companies are being built.

**How We Work:**

Core hours are Monday through Friday, 9 to 6. When we're sprinting toward a demo or field test, the team ramps up — nights, weekends, whatever it takes to ship. When the sprint lands, we ramp down. We don't manufacture intensity for show. If you've worked at SpaceX, against a mission-critical timeline, or on a racing team, you already know the rhythm.

**Benefits:**

* Competitive salary and equity
* United Health Care medical, dental, and vision coverage
* Flexible 18 days PTO plus 5 sick days
* Travel to field test events and range days
* Covered daily lunches and office snacks and drinks
* E-bike and scooter stipend up to $500
* Direct access to leadership and real ownership over your work

**Export Control Notice:**

This role requires access to export-controlled information or items that require U.S. Person status. As defined by U.S. law, individuals who are any one of the following are considered to be a U.S. Person: (1) U.S. citizens, (2) legal permanent residents (a.k.a. green card holders), and (3) certain protected classes of asylees and refugees, as defined in 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

Compensation Range: $145K - $185K

jobs.title: Electrical Engineering Lead
jobs.description:
**About Bridge Neurotech**
--------------------------

Bridge Neurotech is building a non-invasive functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) platform with AI-based neural decoding for brain-computer interface applications. We are a seed-stage neurotechnology company developing technology that has the potential to transform how we interact with the human brain.

**About the role**
------------------

We are looking for an Electrical Engineering Lead to own the architecture strategy and delivery of the electronic systems behind Bridge’s custom ultrasound hardware: from system partitioning and component selection through schematic, layout, bring-up, and validated hardware.

Two design challenges sit at the center of this role. The first is high-speed I/O: moving raw acquisition data off the front-end over multi-gigabit-per-second links, with a focus on designing for signal integrity, clocking, and proper layout. The second is power delivery: multi-rail systems operating at watts of power, designed for efficiency and thermal headroom.

You will interface with ASICs at register level, write Python daily for bring-up and test automation, and know enough firmware to collaborate efficiently with our embedded systems team.

**What you’ll do**
------------------

* Own the end-to-end electronics architecture of Bridge’s custom imaging hardware: system partitioning, component selection, schematic capture, PCB layout oversight, bring-up, and design validation.
* Design and deliver boards with multi-gigabit-per-second serial links (e.g., LVDS, JESD204, PCIe/USB 3.x-class SerDes), owning signal integrity, impedance control, clocking, and high-speed layout.
* Architect watts-class power delivery: multi-rail regulation, sequencing, efficiency, thermal design, and noise isolation for sensitive analog acquisition circuitry.
* Evaluate, select, and integrate ultrasound transmit/receive ASICs and analog front-ends: own the electrical interface to custom silicon and drive vendor relationships.
* Co-define the hardware/software boundary with the Embedded Systems Lead: digital interface definition, control plane, and data path. Write firmware where it accelerates bring-up.
* Build Python-based bring-up, characterization, and automated test tooling for every board revision.
* Lead board bring-up, debug, and failure analysis; manage PCB fabrication and assembly vendors and drive design reviews.
* Mentor the R&D Engineer, reviewing their schematics, layouts, and test methodology.
* Lay the documentation and design-control groundwork for eventual development in a regulated environment.

**Who you are**
---------------

**Required**

* Degree in electrical engineering or related field, with 6+ years of hands-on board-level design experience and multiple custom boards taken through production or production-equivalent builds.
* Extended experience with high-speed digital board design: multi-gigabit-per-second serial links, controlled-impedance routing, and signal/power integrity analysis.
* Demonstrated design of power delivery systems operating at watts of power: switching regulators, multi-rail architectures, sequencing, and thermal management.
* Working understanding of ASICs and how to interface with them: register-level configuration, electrical integration of custom silicon or analog front-ends, and informed dialogue with silicon vendors.
* Enough firmware fluency to write some embedded code yourself and work effectively day-to-day with an embedded systems engineer.
* Good command of Python for bring-up scripts, automated test, and data analysis.
* Experience from consumer electronics or other high-volume consumer products, where cost, manufacturability, and iteration speed were real constraints.

**Nice to have**

* Familiarity with hardware design in regulated environments (e.g., IEC 60601, design controls, medical or similar).
* Prior work on ultrasound, imaging, or other high-channel-count data acquisition front-ends, including AFE/ADC characterization.
* FPGA familiarity, enough to reason about the interface between your boards and programmable logic.
* EMC/EMI pre-compliance and debug experience.
* Early-stage startup experience where you set the hardware roadmap yourself.

**What we offer**
-----------------

* The opportunity to shape a role and a team from the earliest stages.
* Direct collaboration with leading clinicians and neuroscientists at top-tier academic institutions.
* Excellent medical benefits and a 6% match 401(k).

Bridge Neurotech is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply.

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. Monitoring Cloud is seeking engineers to architect, implement, deliver, and operate the telemetry agents and instrumentation libraries that power observability at Salesforce scale.
  
  
Monitoring Cloud is an integral part of the Salesforce Infrastructure, providing the insights every development team relies on to detect and remediate incidents and keep Salesforce products highly available for our customers. This cloud owns the entire telemetry stack, from the agents that emit, collect, and ship telemetry to the large-scale backends that store it and serve low-latency queries. jobs.title: Senior Flight Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**About Poseidon Aerospace:**
-----------------------------

Poseidon Aerospace is reimagining how the world moves goods. We build and operate full-size autonomous cargo aircraft - capable of carrying two tons of payload over a thousand nautical miles. From remote communities to contested logistics operations, our platforms unlock a new cost curve for air freight, making it faster, cheaper, and accessible anywhere it's needed. Headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area with locations in Washington DC, Oregon, and Maine; we're building something consequential.

**About the role**
------------------

Flight software is the code that runs on the flight computers of our autonomous cargo aircraft. As a Senior Flight Software Engineer you will own major parts of that software, from architecture through flight test. You will decide how the software is structured, how it handles failures, and how it is tested, and you will write a large share of the code yourself. You will also set the technical bar for the engineers around you.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Own the architecture of major flight software subsystems, including timing, partitioning, and redundancy
* Design and implement deterministic, real-time embedded flight software in C++
* Design fault detection and response for the aircraft, including redundancy management, degraded modes, and lost-link behavior
* Define software requirements and interfaces with avionics, GNC, and flight test, and trace them to tests
* Implement the GNC team’s algorithms in flight code and verify them against simulation
* Set the test strategy across unit tests, software-in-the-loop, and hardware-in-the-loop
* Build telemetry, logging, and command paths between the aircraft and the ground station
* Lead software integration on the aircraft and support ground testing and flight test, including travel to our flight test site
* Set coding standards and review practices, and lead design reviews
* Mentor other flight software engineers

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* B.S. in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience
* 5+ years of professional C or C++ development on embedded, real-time, or safety-critical systems
* Owned a flight software subsystem or equivalent from architecture through fielded operation
* Took software through hardware integration and test on a real vehicle (aircraft, spacecraft, or automotive)
* Designed fault detection and response for a system where failure had safety consequences
* Led design reviews and set technical direction for other engineers

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Flight software experience on crewed or uncrewed aircraft, or on spacecraft
* RTOS or bare-metal development, with a deep understanding of scheduling, timing, and memory
* Experience designing redundant or fault-tolerant flight computer architectures
* Experience developing software under DO-178C or a comparable standard such as ISO 26262
* Experience supporting flight test or vehicle test campaigns
* Python for tooling, test automation, and flight data analysis
* Clear technical writing

**Why this role**
-----------------

Flight software touches every system on the aircraft: avionics, propulsion, flight controls, and the ground station. You will make the decisions that shape how those systems work together, at a stage where the architecture is still yours to set. You will work directly with flight hardware and watch your code fly an aircraft that carries two tons.

**What you get from us**
------------------------

* Competitive salary and meaningful early-stage equity
* Relocation support if applicable
* Employee Health Benefit Plans
* 6% Retirement matching
* Flexible PTO
* Free lunches, snacks, and a stocked fridge at our offices
* AI tools and subscriptions

jobs.description:
**Company:**

**Job Area:**

Engineering Group, Engineering Group > Modem Software Engineering

**General Summary:**

Qualcomm is a company of inventors that unlocked 5G — ushering in an age of rapid acceleration in connectivity and new possibilities that will transform industries, create jobs, and enrich lives. But this is just the beginning. It takes inventive minds with diverse skills, backgrounds, and cultures to transform 5G's potential into world-changing technologies and products. This is the Invention Age — and this is where you come in.

  
  

The MMODE team develops protocol software that enables intelligent system selection and mobility across terrestrial and satellite wireless networks. MMODE software determines how devices discover, select, acquire, and transition between available connectivity options while balancing user experience, network performance, power efficiency, and operator requirements. Engineers work on technologies including 5G NR, LTE, NTN, Multi-SIM, emergency services, and next-generation connectivity solutions, collaborating closely with systems, modem firmware, and test teams to deliver innovative wireless features.

  
  

As a Modem Software Engineer, you will design, develop, and optimize real-time embedded software for Qualcomm's modem subsystem (MPSS). You will work close to the metal — writing performant, resource-constrained C/C++ that runs on DSP and Arm cores across cellular protocol layers, device drivers, and RTOS-level components.

  
  

Beyond traditional embedded development, this role is explicitly **AI-native** . You are expected to leverage, build, and improve AI-assisted development workflows — using code-generation agents, LLM-based code review, automated test synthesis, log/crash triage assistants, and retrieval-augmented tooling over our codebase — to dramatically accelerate delivery, quality, and debugging in a highly complex firmware environment.

  
  

**Principal Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Design, implement, and optimize **real-time embedded modem software** across protocol layers, drivers, and platform services, meeting strict latency, memory, and power constraints.
* Apply rigorous **data-structure and algorithm** design to build efficient, scalable firmware components.
* Own end-to-end feature delivery: requirements, architecture, implementation, unit/integration testing, on-target bring-up, and maintenance.
* **Pioneer AI-native development practices** within the team — integrate AI coding agents into daily workflows, establish agent rules and prompt patterns, and measurably reduce development and debug cycle time.
* Build and maintain **AI-assisted tooling** for code review, static analysis, test synthesis, and automated crash/log triage over the modem codebase.
* Debug and root-cause complex, multi-layer issues on target hardware, increasingly leveraging AI-assisted analysis of logs, traces, and RAM dumps.
* Collaborate cross-functionally with systems, hardware, test, and integration teams to deliver production-quality modem firmware.
* Contribute to code reviews, design reviews, and continuous improvement of engineering standards — including standards for the responsible and effective use of AI in the SDLC.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Agentic Runtime
jobs.description:
**About Glean:**

Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.

At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.

Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality.

If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

**About the Role:**

The Agentic Runtime team builds the low‑latency, reliable, and secure foundation that powers Glean’s AI agents and assistant experiences at scale. You’ll design and operate core runtime services for multi‑turn orchestration, tool calling, model routing, memory, streaming, and safety. You’ll work across distributed systems, production observability, and ML infra integrations to deliver an experience that feels instant, accurate, and trustworthy — while optimizing cost and reliability.

**You will:**

* Own impactful runtime problems end‑to‑end — from architecture and design to production launch and ongoing reliability.
* Build and evolve core services for session lifecycle, streaming responses (e.g., gRPC/WebSockets), structured tool execution, memory/state, and policy/guardrails.
* Design for performance, correctness, and cost: reduce p50/p95 latency, improve tail behavior, and optimize token/tool budgets.
* Integrate with leading LLM providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) and internal evaluation frameworks to improve quality and predictability.
* Harden the platform with fault isolation, retries, timeouts, circuit‑breaking, backpressure, and graceful degradation.
* Instrument deep observability (tracing, metrics, logs) and create playbooks/SLOs for high availability and on‑call excellence.
* Collaborate closely with product, quality, and application teams to prioritize the most impactful roadmap investments.

**You are:**

* 3+ years of software engineering experience building production distributed systems or cloud‑native applications.
* BS/BA in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Strong coding skills in at least one of: Python, Go, Java, Javascript, Typescript, C++, with a focus on reliability, performance, and tests.
* Product‑minded: you prioritize customer impact, clear SLAs/SLOs, and pragmatic iteration.
* Ownership‑driven with a positive, proactive attitude; comfortable leading projects or learning from battle‑tested engineers.

* Experience operating services on Kubernetes and at least one major cloud (e.g., GCP, AWS, or Azure).
* Familiarity with event/streaming systems (e.g., Pub/Sub, Kafka), caching (e.g., Redis), and data stores for low‑latency paths.
* Practical understanding of LLM/agents building blocks: tool/function calling, structured outputs, streaming, and model selection/routing.
* Strong observability and debugging skills: tracing (e.g., OpenTelemetry), metrics, dashboards, and production forensics.
* Background in one or more areas is a plus: policy/guardrails, multi‑tenant isolation, rate‑limiting, concurrency control, cost optimization.

**Location:**

* This role is hybrid (4 days a week in our Mountain View office)

**Compensation & Benefits:**

The standard base salary range for this position is $180,000 - $210,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. Neon Aero is seeking a Principal Electrical Engineer in Irvine, California. The Principal Engineer, High Voltage Power Electronics for Motor Drives provides technical leadership in the architecture, design, and qualification of high voltage motor drives for aerospace and advanced mobility applications. This is a deeply hands-on role: the engineer personally develops architectures, block diagrams, schematics, and the analysis behind them, and owns the rationale for every major design decision across drives from 1 kW to 100 kW, on DC buses from 270 V to 800 V (up to 1000 V), powered by batteries in applications such as eVTOL and by turbogenerator systems. The role collaborates closely with motor control, embedded software, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, and supply chain teams, and provides strong technical leadership, ownership, and mentoring of other engineers without direct people management responsibility.

**Key Responsibilities**

Architecture and Power Stage Design

* Own architecture and design of HV motor drives in two classes: 1 to 3 kW convection-cooled, and 3 to 100 kW liquid or forced-air cooled.
* Design inverter power stages for 270 V to 800 V buses (up to 1000 V): device selection (SiC, GaN, Si), gate drive, protection, and sensing.
* Develop PMSM drive hardware, applying motor control fundamentals to select feedback sensors, current sensing, switching frequency, and processors.
* Design input DM/CM filters and size DC link capacitors for ripple, stability, and lifetime.

EMI, Grounding, and Thermal Design

* Define shielding, grounding, and bonding for motors, cables, and enclosures to contain switching noise.
* Own thermal and EMI design for integrated motor and controller units in a single enclosure.
* Select components, processors, and HV connectors for high-vibration, extended-temperature aviation and defense environments.

Analysis, Validation, and Qualification

* Personally perform loss, thermal, stress, derating, insulation, EMI, and worst-case analyses.
* Develop schematics and review layouts for high dv/dt power stages (creepage, clearance, commutation loops, partial discharge).
* Lead bring-up, validation, and root cause investigations in the lab.
* Support DO-160 and MIL-STD-461 qualification and transition designs into production.

Manufacturing and Mentorship

* Drive DFM, DFT, and DFA; define manufacturing test requirements, coverage, and end-of-line test strategy.
* Mentor EEs developing 28 V and 48 V motor drive controllers.

**Qualifications**

* BS or MS in Electrical Engineering or related field; equivalent experience considered.
* Minimum of 12 years designing and shipping power electronics, including multiple motor drives or high power converters.
* Hands-on design experience at both low power (1 to 3 kW) and high power (up to about 100 kW).
* Direct experience with HV DC buses (270 V to 800 V, up to 1000 V).
* Depth in at least one of automotive, industrial, aviation, or defense at comparable complexity.
* Expertise in inverter power stages, device selection, gate drive, DC link, and EMI filter design.
* Working knowledge of PMSM drives, FOC, feedback sensors, and current sensing.
* Strong grounding, shielding, and noise containment practice for motor, cable, and enclosure systems.
* Proficiency with Altium (or equivalent) and circuit simulation (SPICE, PLECS, or similar).

Preferred Experience

* SiC or GaN power stage design at high dv/dt and high switching frequency.
* Electric propulsion, eVTOL, hybrid-electric, or turbogenerator systems.

* Insulation coordination and partial discharge at altitude for high voltage aircraft systems.

**What We Value**

jobs.title: Deep Learning Software Engineer, TensorRT Performance - New College Grad 2027
jobs.description:
We are now looking for a Deep Learning Software Engineer, TensorRT Performance! NVIDIA is seeking an experienced Deep Learning Engineer passionate about analyzing and improving the performance of NVIDIA’s inference ecosystem! NVIDIA is rapidly growing our research and development for Deep Learning Inference and is seeking excellent Software Engineers at all levels of expertise to join our team. Companies around the world are using NVIDIA GPUs to power a revolution in deep learning, enabling breakthroughs in areas like Generative AI, Recommenders and Vision that have put DL into every software solution. Join the team that builds the software to enable the performance optimization, deployment and serving of these DL inference solutions. We specialize in developing GPU-accelerated deep learning inference software like TensorRT, DL benchmarking software and performant solutions to deploy and serve these models.

Collaborate with the deep learning community to integrate TensorRT into OSS frameworks like TensorRT-EdgeLLM and PyTorch. Identify performance opportunities and optimize SoTA models across the spectrum of NVIDIA accelerators, from datacenter GPUs to edge SoCs. Implement graph compiler algorithms, frontend operators and code generators across NVIDIA’s inference ecosystem. Work and collaborate with a diverse set of teams involving workflow improvements, performance modeling, performance analysis, kernel development and inference software development.

**What you'll be doing:**

* Establish groundbreaking performance benchmarking methodologies and analysis workflows and identify performance issues and opportunities for NVIDIA’s inference ecosystem (e.g. TensorRT/TensorRT-EdgeLLM/Torch-TensorRT)
* Contribute features and code to NVIDIA/OSS inference frameworks including but not limited to TensorRT/TensorRT-EdgeLLM/Torch-TensorRT.
* Develop new model pipelines for NVIDIA’s inference ecosystem with optimized performance including but not limited to areas like quantization, scheduling, memory management, and distributed inference to set the gold standard for Gen AI performance.
* Work with cross-collaborative teams inside and outside of NVIDIA across generative AI, automotive, robotics, image understanding, and speech understanding to set directions and develop innovative inference solutions.
* Scale performance of deep learning models across different architectures and types of NVIDIA accelerators.

**What we need to see:**

* Bachelors, Masters, PhD, or equivalent experience in relevant fields (Computer Science, Computer Engineering, EECS, AI).
* 2 years of relevant software development experience.
* Strong C++, Python programming and software engineering skills
* Experience with DL frameworks (e.g. PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, ONNX) and inference libraries (e.g. TensorRT, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, SGLang, FlashInfer).
* Experience with performance analysis and performance optimization

**Ways to stand out from the crowd:**

* Strong foundation and architectural knowledge of GPUs.
* Deep understanding of modern deep learning models and workloads (e.g. Transformers, Recommenders, ASR, TTS, Visual Understanding).
* Proficiency in one of the deep learning programming domain specific languages (e.g. CUDA/TileIR/CuTeDSL/cutlass/Triton).
* Prior contributions to major LLM inference frameworks (e.g. vLLM) or prior experience with graph compilers in deep learning inference (e.g. TorchDynamo/TorchInductor).
* Prior experience optimizing performance for low-latency, resource-constrained systems or embedded AI pipelines (e.g. Jetson systems or other edge AI accelerators).

GPU deep learning has provided the foundation for machines to learn, perceive, reason and solve problems posed using human language. The GPU started out as the engine for simulating human imagination, conjuring up the amazing virtual worlds of video games and Hollywood films. Now, NVIDIA's GPU runs deep learning algorithms, simulating human intelligence, and acts as the brain of computers, robots and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world. Just as human imagination and intelligence are linked, computer graphics and artificial intelligence come together in our architecture. Two modes of the human brain, two modes of the GPU. This may explain why NVIDIA GPUs are used broadly for deep learning, and NVIDIA is increasingly known as “the AI computing company.” Come, join our DL Architecture team, where you can help build a real-time, cost-effective computing platform driving our success in this exciting and quickly growing field.

jobs.title: Flight Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
**Flight Systems Engineering and Test**

SiFly Aviation · Santa Clara, CA · Onsite · Full-time

At SiFly, we're building a new category of aircraft: vertical-takeoff, long-endurance drones that deliver helicopter-level performance at drone economics. After thousands of flight tests and years of engineering, our NDAA-compliant platform flies more than 2 hours in hover or 3 hours in forward flight on a single charge — matching the capability of traditional helicopters at a fraction of their cost and operational burden. We merge aerial robotics, perception, and onboard intelligence to cut complexity and minimize human intervention, and our unique approach to communications and networking unlocks remote operations from day one. It's an ambitious mission, and we're a small team that moves fast.

**The role**

We fly a lot – and are building methodical ways of turning data from flights into evolved control system decisions. You’ll design test flight campaigns for the questions we need to answer and develop instrumentation that produces trustworthy data. You’ll drive and develop dashboards that tell us whether weight, performance, and reliability are moving the right way.

You'll also be a large part of how we tune and validate changes to PX4 — configuration and code — and how the resulting data gets back to the engineers who need it.

**What you'll do**

* Plan and execute test campaigns end to end — objectives, success criteria, test cards, instrumentation, and safety and site coordination.
* Choose the right validation modality for each question: simulation, log replay, hardware-in-the-loop, ground test, or flight. Spend flight time on the highest-value learning.
* Tune and test changes to PX4 — parameters, control and estimation tuning, and configuration — and validate them in the air.
* Analyze flight logs and telemetry to diagnose issues across firmware, hardware, and companion computers.
* Build and maintain test infrastructure: benches, HIL setups, instrumentation, and the data pipelines and dashboards behind them.
* Own the progression from bench test, through integrated ground runs, to flight — and the anomaly reports and configuration records that make a campaign reconstructable.
* Generate the flight test evidence used in SiFly’s FAA submissions.
* Find, build, and share AI-assisted approaches to this work — log analysis, test data reduction, reporting — and bring the team along with what works.

**What we're looking for**

* Hands-on flight test or systems test on real aircraft, manned or unmanned. You build test setups, not just operate them.
* You've closed the loop from controls systems or flight data back into autopilot parameters or code, repeatedly, on real equipment.
* Estimation and control fundamentals: coordinate frames, Kalman filtering and sensor fusion, PID analysis.
* Data analysis and scripting — Python or equivalent — for reducing test data into something people act on.
* Comfortable at the aircraft: instrumentation, harnessing, and debugging on the flight line.
* Ability to obtain and use FAA Part 107 certification if not already certified.
* First-principles thinking and a drive to understand the “why” behind traditional approaches to propulsion, power systems, and even radio technologies.
* This is a hands-on job at a company that is still small. You'll be at the bench, in the shop, on the flight line, and sometimes at a customer site working out why a deployed system is misbehaving — alongside new product development.
* You use AI as a real tool, not a talking point. We want to hear one specific example of something you did with AI that surprised you — a workflow you rebuilt, a problem you came at sideways, an analysis that wouldn't have been worth doing by hand. We care less about which tools you use than about what you've changed about how you work. We're enthusiastic about the leverage and unforgiving about errors.

**Nice to have**

* Existing FAA Part 107 certification and real drone piloting or field-testing experience.
* Flight test instrumentation design — sensors, DAQ, wiring and installation for test.
* ROS 2, MAVSDK, Linux companion computers; safety risk management process for flight testing.

**Details**

* Onsite in Santa Clara, CA.
* Small team, high ownership, and real hardware in the building.

Bridge Neurotech is building a non-invasive functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) platform with AI-based neural decoding for brain-computer interface applications. We are a seed-stage neurotechnology company developing technology that has the potential to transform how we interact with the human brain.

**About the role**
------------------

We are looking for a Hardware Engineer to turn ideas into physical parts, and to turn the making of those parts into a repeatable process. Almost nothing we build can be bought, so we need to build our own as one-off or low-volume production. You will own that work: design it, build it, test it, scale it.

This is a hands-on lab role with significant breadth: CAD in the morning, soldering in the afternoon, and Python scripting in between. We expect you to use AI coding tools to develop automations and bespoke tools to improve efficiency.

**What you’ll do**
------------------

* Design and iterate mechanical part design in CAD, for example probe housings, mounts, fixtures, enclosures, and lab hardware.
* Own our 3D printing: run and maintain the printers, dial in materials and profiles, manage the queue, and keep turnaround measured in hours.
* Build the workflow and automation around 3D printing and CNC, for example scripted slicing and job submission, print farm monitoring, CAM setup, revision control, and part tracking.
* Develop processes for low-volume part production, for example mold design and fabrication, casting, potting, bonding, finishing, and the jigs and fixtures those processes need.
* Do the work that makes hardware real: fine-pitch and through-hole soldering, cable and harness assembly, routing, and careful assembly of delicate parts.
* Build and maintain test fixtures and benchtop setups, and keep lab equipment calibrated, organized, and working.
* Write Python to glue the shop together: automation, instrument control, data logging, and part and inventory tracking.
* Support the team’s everyday hardware needs, for example specifying and ordering equipment, setting up workstations and lab machines, and keeping the shop stocked.
* Work directly with our imaging scientists and research team to understand how each part will actually be used.

**Who you are**
---------------

**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
* Working proficiency in CAD: parametric modeling, assemblies, drawings, and design for manufacturing.
* Hands-on 3D printing experience, for example tuning, troubleshooting, and repair, plus the judgment to know when a part should be printed, machined, or molded.
* Strong technician skills: comfortable soldering both boards and wire, building clean harnesses, and assembling precision hardware without breaking it.
* Demonstrated experience with Python. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to write a real script, for example file handling, an API call, a serial interface, some data wrangling, without it being a project.
* Fluent with AI coding tools and comfortable vibe coding your way to working tooling.
* A bias toward building, testing, and improving over designing to completion first.
* Self-directed and self-motivated, with the ability to execute on a goal rather than a step-by-step guide.

**Nice to have**

* PCB layout experience, particularly in Altium.
* CNC machining experience, for example CAM programming, fixturing, workholding.
* IT and lab infrastructure work, for example specifying and ordering computers, installing software, and managing network and lab equipment.
* Personal projects, a shop of your own, robotics or FSAE, or other evidence that you build things unprompted.
* Prior work in a startup or small team, or other evidence of thriving without much scaffolding.

**What we offer**
-----------------

* Real ownership of the hardware this company runs on, with a direct path to growing into a senior or lead role as the team scales.
* A shop you get to build. We buy the equipment and tooling; you decide what we need and how it runs.
* Direct collaboration with our imaging scientists and research team, and with leading clinicians and neuroscientists at top-tier academic institutions.
* Work on a modality early enough that the tooling does not exist yet. Much of what you build will be the first of its kind.
* Excellent medical benefits and a 6% match 401(k).

Bridge Neurotech is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply.

**Title:**

Software Engineer - Real-Time Geospatial Mapping for Planetary Exploration  
  

At KBR, we deliver science, technology and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world. KBR employs approximately 37,000 people worldwide with customers in more than 85 countries and operations in over 28 countries. Backed by decades of mission success, deep expertise, and trusted partnerships, Trinzic will launch as a global organization with more than 18,000 employees supporting customers around the world. Join us at a defining moment and help shape the future of a company built to tackle complex challenges and make a meaningful impact.

  
  

*Candidates who join KBR's Mission Technology Solutions business before the spin-off will transition to Trinzic when the separation is complete and will not need to reapply for employment.*

  

BELONG. CONNECT. GROW. with KBR.

Around here, we define the future. We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

**Description of work effort:**

Join NASA Ames writing software to help explore the moon! Help us meet the emerging needs of Artemis, Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) and future Moon-to-Mars missions. Looking for a software engineer to assist with development of two coordinated work efforts:

* **M2M CSDS** - the Moon to Mars Collaborative Science Data System
* **WITME** - Web-Based Integrated Terrain Model Estimation tool

These tools provide a reusable, science-centric collaboration platform that enables distributed science teams to collectively visualize, analyze, and interpret mission data in support of time-critical decision making. They will prototype capability for uncertainty-aware fusion of orbital and surface terrain data for real-time operational decision support.

M2M CSDS and WITME both build on NASA Ames - developed collaborative data systems and science operations architectures matured through the Exploration Ground Data Systems (xGDS) research project and VIPER mission science operations.

M2M CSDS development will require the applicant to work closely with an active CLPS science team to populate the proof-of-concept M2M CSDS with mission relevant data. Software development will include an interactive, shared planning/replanning and execution monitoring capability that builds on design concepts developed for the Ames-led xGDS in a mature mission-proven environment. The work effort will include the integration of FedRAMP and NASA approved AI tools (e.g. Google Gemini) to provide summarization and search capabilities on the data sets and annotations deployed in M2M CSDS. These capabilities are anticipated to provide substantial benefits for supporting real-time science and operations (e.g. rapid initial generation of shift handover highlights that can be further augmented and edited by science team members).

WITME involves the development and application of statistically principled fusion methods to weight orbital and surface data by their uncertainties, and build unified 3D models with quantitative confidence estimates derived from these data. Specifically, the applicant will help develop effective user interfaces and displays to communicate confidence in terrain model data at different locations. This will enable mission teams to rapidly assimilate new terrain data, improving traverse planning and decision-making through a collaborative web-based interface.

**Required Experience & Skills**

***\*\*Must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident\*\****

*Web Development:* Expertise in JavaScript including at least one common JavaScript MVC framework (e.g., Vue, React, Bootstrap, or Angular)

* *UI/UX* *Proficiency*: experience with user-facing application design and implementation. Familiar with modern standards and best practices in UI design and development (responsive design, ADA compliance).
* Proficient in utilizing server-side services, APIs and database tools and understanding how they interface with complex JavaScript applications.
* *JavaScript Mapping/Rendering:* An understanding of 2D geographic mapping libraries such as OpenLayers, CesiumJS, Three, Leaflet, Google Maps API, etc
* *Geographic Map Projections:* Familiarity with using different map projections and coordinate systems.
* *Geographic Map Services:* Familiarity with services that provide map layers such as Google or Bing Maps, MapBox or any WMS data provider/ DEMs.
* *3D Graphics:* Experience with 3D graphics, particularly as used with terrain mapping (e.g. DEMs) and a practical understanding of the underlying mathematical concepts used in graphics

**Areas of Desired Experience & Skills**

**About Radiant**
-----------------

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based startup building the world’s first mass-produced, portable nuclear microreactors. The company’s first reactor, Kaleidos, is a 1-megawatt, fail-safe microreactor that can be transported anywhere power is needed and run for up to 5 years without refueling. Portable nuclear power with rapid-deploy capability can replace similar-sized diesel generators and provide critical asset support for hospitals, data centers, remote sites, and military bases. Radiant’s unique, practical approach to nuclear development leverages modern software engineering to rapidly deliver safe, factory-built microreactors that use existing, well-qualified materials. Founded in 2020, Radiant is on track to test its first reactor at the Idaho National Laboratory this summer, with initial customer deliveries beginning in 2028.

**About the Role**
------------------

Radiant is seeking a highly motivated **Staff Fluid Systems Engineer** to own critical Kaleidos fluid systems from preliminary design through build and production. These systems include the primary loop subsystems and power conversion loop, serving to convert heat from the reactor core into electrical power. You will be responsible for the following: trade studies, component selection, thermal hydraulic analysis, piping design, vendor selection, assembly, and testing. jobs.description:
San Mateo, CA, United StatesEngineeringID: 46543

  

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device.We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

**Why Roblox & Agent Infra**
----------------------------

The Agent Infra team builds the infrastructure that runs autonomous AI agents at Roblox for millions of creators building experiences on our platform, and for thousands of Roblox engineers shipping production code every day.

Agent workloads break the assumptions most infrastructure is built on. They run for hours instead of milliseconds, they’re non-deterministic, they execute code nobody wrote, and they need real credentials against real systems to be useful at all. Making that safe, durable, and cost-effective at Roblox’s scale is the hard problem our team is solving.

As an early member of the Agent Infra team, you’ll work alongside an experienced engineering team on systems that are already in front of real users, at scale, in a field that didn’t exist two years ago.

**You Are**
-----------

* **Demonstrated experience:** 8+ years building and operating backend, distributed, or infrastructure systems in production, including systems you designed that held up at scale for years.
* **Deep expertise** in at least one of our core domains: workflow orchestration, scalable backend infrastructure, agentic runtimes, or secure sandboxing and access.
* **Hands-on:** You spend most of your time building, and you write production code in Go, Python, Rust, or similar.
* **Agent-native:** Agents drive your daily work. You’ve experimented with swarms, loops, and orchestration, you have strong opinions on harness and model choice, and you’re constantly evolving your agentic workflow.
* **Experienced with agents in production:** You’ve run agents against real systems, seen how they fail, and know what the infrastructure underneath should do about it.
* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a similar technical field.

**You Will**
------------

* **Set the technical direction:** Own the design and implementation of Roblox’s core agent infrastructure, and scale it to serve every internal and external customer.
* **Drive reliability and security:** Keep long-running agents alive through deploys, restarts, and outages. Run untrusted code in sandboxes that keep credentials out of the agent’s reach and control what it can reach on the network. Define the SLOs and observability that hold the platform to account.
* **Raise the bar:** Keep learning and experimenting with agentic workflows, and bring what works to the team and the wider Foundation AI org.
* **Align across the org:** Partner with Security, Engineering Efficiency, and Infrastructure so the agent platform and the systems it depends on are built in the same direction.
* **Multiply the team:** Mentor senior engineers, lead design reviews, and push how far agents can build the agent platform itself.

**Nice to Have**
----------------

* Security experience with systems that run untrusted code: sandbox and container isolation (gVisor, Firecracker, microVMs), Kubernetes hardening, network segmentation and egress control.
* Experience working with Temporal, AWS, and self-hosted models.
* Experience building and deploying production systems on Kubernetes, using GitOps and Argo CD.
* Contributions to open source or experience building your own product with real user traction.

**Sierra Space Careers:**

At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.

Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.

Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.

We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.

**About the Role**

The Senior Flight Software Engineer role at Sierra Space brings extensive experience and deep expertise to the design, development, and architecture of complex safety critical software systems. jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer, Payload Platform (BSP & Fabric), Project Sunrise
jobs.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE), supporting Blue Origin’s mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. The team fosters innovation and drives engineering workflows of the future, shared solutions and standards, simplicity and lower costs, and manufacturable design.

*Join Blue Origin as we build infrastructure in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re developing a satellite constellation of orbital data centers, Sunrise, designed to transform how compute infrastructure is deployed and leveraged.*

**Job Summary:** Our team is developing next-generation spacecraft that push the boundaries of performance and capability in orbit. We are seeking a highly skilled platform software engineer to own the Board Support Package (BSP) and fabric bring-up for our accelerator compute payloads. You will be responsible for the lowest layers of the software stack—the code that makes the hardware work. This includes everything from the bootloader and Linux kernel to driver initialization and fabric management. This is a role for a deep, hands-on expert who is comfortable debugging complex hardware interactions in a remote, no-hands-on environment and who is passionate about building a reliable, high-performance computing platform for space.

**Responsibilities include but are not limited to:**

* Develop and own the Board Support Package (BSP) for our accelerator compute modules, including the bootloader, Linux kernel bring-up, device drivers, high-speed interconnect enumeration, and the hardware abstraction layer (HAL).
* Lead the software bring-up and validation of the high-speed compute fabric, including configuring fabric management software and validating GPU-to-GPU collective communications.
* Implement and manage robust, in-flight health monitoring systems for the compute payload, tracking accelerator temperatures, ECC error rates, power draw, and interconnect performance.
* Design and implement automated recovery mechanisms to handle radiation-induced soft errors and ensure system resilience.
* Define and maintain the API boundaries between the platform software and higher-level services, including the inference runtime and job orchestration layers.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
* 6+ years of experience in embedded Linux Board Support Package (BSP) or low-level platform software development.
* Direct, hands-on experience with the software bring-up and validation of accelerator hardware (e.g., GPUs, TPUs) is required.
* High proficiency in C/C++ and Python for embedded systems.
* Familiarity with GPU programming models (e.g., CUDA, ROCm) and collective communication libraries (e.g., NCCL, RCCL).
* Proven experience debugging hardware at the driver/firmware layer in an environment with limited observability.
* Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s or Ph.D. in a relevant discipline.
* 10+ years of relevant experience.
* Deep experience with fabric management software for large-scale accelerator clusters is a strong differentiator.
* Proven ability to work effectively with pre-silicon emulation platforms, FPGAs, or early-stage reference hardware before final hardware is available.
* Experience designing software for high-reliability, fault-tolerant, or remote/inaccessible systems.
Passion for and understanding of AI and Machine Learning applications in engineering, with a demonstrated ability to learn and integrate new technologies  

  

Base Pay Range for:

CO applicants is $181,626.00 - $254,275.35
WA applicants is $197,529.00 - $276,539.55

**Other site ranges may differ**

  

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

  

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

  

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Application deadline: Oct 17, 2026  
  
We're building the Gen AI–powered platform that takes a Devices product idea from concept to production in days — not months.
  
  
The Devices Global Retail Tech organization is looking for a Principal Software Engineer to lead diverse, cross-organizational initiatives spanning Devices financial systems automation, product development acceleration, and multi-agent orchestration architectures. As the most senior individual contributor, you will work on our hardest problems, help establish technical standards, NativeAI development practices, and drive the overall technical architecture for products that delight our customers.
  
  
The Devices Financial System Automation (DFSA) team owns the consolidated technical architecture that transforms how Devices & Services (D&S) businesses set up and operate their financial systems. D&S launches a fast-growing portfolio — Alexa, Fire TV, Ring, Blink, eero, Kindle, Appstore, Amazon Smart Vehicles, and more — and every new business launch requires financial record-keeping (FRK) setup spanning the entire fintech domains from contract review, business requirements, tax classification, accounting entries, billing and payments. DFSA partners with teams across the Amazon's D&S division to accelerate new product launches.
  
  
Architecting agentic primitives at scale is central to our strategy. We are building a Gen AI–powered automation platform that takes a product idea or partner deal from initial idea to a live, automated financial record-keeping capabilities in days to weeks — using large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and multi-agent orchestration workflows. These solutions draft contracts, requirements, engineering specifications, and code that previously took teams months to produce. As Principal Engineer, you will define and drive the multi-year, architecture for this platform: unifying fragmented workflows into scalable, flexible, and compliant FinTech solutions, and setting the technical direction for how Gen AI is applied safely and accurately across financial systems. This is a strategic investment adopted not just by the Devices & Services organization, but also teams across Digital, Ads and Consumer groups. You will shape the strategy that accelerates timelines from months to days, enabling every D&S business to launch and monetize faster.  
  
Another core dependency for accelerating Devices product development lifecycle from months to days requires providing agentic and builder access to Amazon's diverse portfolio of Devices throughout the build process. We provide 16 businesses across Devices, Ads, and Digital teams elastic device capacity and operate as the singular entry point for every device type and setup at Amazon. Amazon Device Farm services provide the device signal that fuels the fast feedback loops autonomous agentic systems and builders need for product development - providing agents and builders unified, elastic device capacity, configured on demand, with the functionality, reliability, and scale teams require to ship products to customers faster and to higher quality.
  
  
As a core leader in the Devices Global Retail Tech org, you'll work to simplify and accelerate Devices and Services product launches across every Product Line (FireTV, Kindle, Alexa, echo, eero, Leo, and more) as well as key partners in Digital, Ads and Consumer teams by driving the architecture and agentic solutions that remove existing constraints spanning diverse problem domains.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
As a Principal Software Engineer, you will:  
  

* Serve as a technical leader on our most demanding, cross-functional projects, owning the consolidated, Gen AI–powered system architecture that solves key fintech problems across all of D&S and Set the technical vision and direction for the org's fintech space

  

* Functionally decompose complex problems into simple, straightforward solutions — designing for reuse across 12+ product lines and multiple geographies rather than one-off integrations.

  

* Possess and apply expert knowledge in performance, scalability, enterprise system architecture, and engineering best practices, with financial accuracy, auditability, and tax/regulatory compliance treated as first-class architectural concerns — ensuring Gen AI outputs are grounded, verifiable, and compliant.

  

* Understand the evolving needs of the D&S business and partner deeply with stakeholders across Business Development, Finance, Product, Tech, Accounting, and Tax to translate those needs into durable technical strategy.

  

* Exert technical influence over multiple teams, increasing their productivity and effectiveness by sharing your deep knowledge and experience. You are a technical thought leader, builder, and operator.

  

* Balance technical leadership and savvy with strong business judgment to make the right decisions about technology choices, sequencing a pragmatic roadmap that delivers incremental value while converging on the target-state consolidated system.

  

* Assist in the career development of others, actively mentoring individuals and the community on advanced technical issues — including Gen AI engineering best practices — and helping managers guide the career growth of their team members.

* 12+ years of software development experience, including designing and delivering large-scale distributed systems.

  

* Experience serving as a technical leader across product and tech teams, driving architecture and technical strategy.

  

* Expert knowledge of performance, scalability, and enterprise system architecture.

  

* Demonstrated ability to influence senior technical and business stakeholders and align diverse teams behind a common direction.

The ideal candidate should have deep knowledge and experience in most of the following studies at the EHV level:

* Shunt Reactive Compensation and Voltage Control
* Coupled Line Resonance Studies (stuck pole on breakers drives NGR size on switched/fixed line connected shunt reactors to prevent resonance)
* Single Pole Automatic Reclosing (NGR sizing, reclose dead time determination, check stability margins, etc)
* Series Capacitor Analysis (develop cap size, MOV sizing, etc.)
* Line Switching Overvoltage Studies (with/without breaker PIRs and point on wave controllers, etc)
* Line Insulation Coordination Studies (includes assessing line clearances and make recommendations for PIRs, sub/line arresters, changes to clearances)
* Breaker TRV/RRRV Studies
* Line or Sub MAD calculations
* Coupling to Adjacent Circuits in ROW
* Voltage/Current Unbalance/Transposition Studies
* Transformer Energization
* TOV studies in HV/EHV systems
* EHV Capacitor Switching (analysis and TLI/PIR sizing)
* Technoeconomic Conductor Selection Studies
* EHV Power Cable Studies (EMT studies of riser design including grounding, cross-bonding, SVL sizing/placement, protection of cables)

The engineer will join a team of experienced engineers and perform detailed EMT analysis for the study work as well as provide guidance to younger staff who this individual will train. Extensive experience with PSCAD is required and knowledge of common loadflow tools, MathCad, Excel is a must.

**Electrical Controls Engineer**

Position Type: Full-time, Exempt, Salary

Reports to: Director Electrical Controls and Strategy

Location: Jacksonville, FL

**Company Summary**

Stellar Energy is a trusted provider of turnkey liquid-to-chip cooling solutions for the world’s leading data center and industrial manufacturing customers. As computing demand and industrial processes continue to grow, modern facilities require cooling infrastructure that can scale quickly, efficiently, and reliably.

Our modular approach enables high-volume production while maintaining the flexibility to customize each solution. From Central Utility Plants to Coolant Distribution Units, Stellar Energy delivers scalable cooling infrastructure designed to support the rapid expansion of data centers and mission-critical industrial operations.

Backed by deep engineering expertise and large-scale manufacturing capability, Stellar Energy helps customers deploy critical infrastructure faster and with confidence.

Do you want to play a direct role in programming and automating the technology that cools the digital world? If so, we invite you to join us in boldly challenging what’s possible for sustainable energy infrastructure.

**Summary Objective**

The Electrical Controls Engineer is responsible for developing, programming, and integrating the control systems and automation logic that run our custom modular chillers. This role focuses on programmable logic controller (PLC) programming, human-machine interface (HMI) development, and establishing robust communication networks between our chillers and the overarching data center management systems (BMS/EPMS).

Responsibilities include creating control sequence of operations, designing low-voltage control panel layouts, defining instrumentation integration (sensors, actuators, transmitters), and ensuring seamless software-to-hardware communication.

**Essential Functions**

* Controls & PLC Programming: Develop, write, and debug PLC ladder logic and structured text codes for chiller plant automation systems (e.g., Rockwell Automation, Siemens, or Carel).
* HMI Design: Program and design intuitive Human-Machine Interface (HMI) screens to allow clear monitoring and operation of modular chiller variables on-site.
* Network Integration: Set up, configure, and troubleshoot industrial communication protocols such as Modbus, BACnet, Ethernet/IP, and Profibus.
* Control Panel Layouts: Design low-voltage control circuits, sensor loops, wire routing, and digital/analog I/O schematics.
* System Integration Support: Assist manufacturing and commissioning teams during the electrical startup and initial "dry-loop" software loading of the modular control panel.
* Travel Requirement: Travel to customer sites for critical control integration, testing, or field startups may be required.

*Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

* Automation Focus: Strong passion for industrial automation, HVAC control sequences, and thermodynamic process controls.

* Standards & Schematics: Ability to read, interpret, and design electrical schematics and control P&IDs in accordance with UL 508A and NEC standards.
* Communication Protocols: Basic knowledge of industrial networks (TCP/IP, serial communication, and client/server architectures).
* Self-Starter: Ability to troubleshoot and trace signal paths systematically from software command to physical field device.

**Work Location**

Most work is performed in an office environment or from client sites. Regular trips to SEA Fabrication Shop for observation and research are required.

**Physical Demands**  
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit. The employee frequently is required to walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand. The employee must frequently lift or move objects up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift or move objects up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision and the ability to adjust focus.

**Travel**  
Anticipated up to 10% travel to customer sites for this position.

**Required Education and Experience.**

* Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls/Automation Engineering, or Computer Engineering.
* Experience: Prior control systems engineering internship, co-op, or 1–2 years of PLC programming/industrial automation experience is required.

**Work Authorization**  
Must be authorized to work in the USA.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role supports the development and operations of New Glenn, a single-configuration, heavy-lift orbital launch vehicle capable of routinely carrying people and payloads to low-Earth orbit, geostationary transfer orbit, cislunar, and beyond. Its first stage is fully reusable, and the vehicle was designed from the beginning to be human-capable.

As part of a small team, you will work on New Glenn at the system level for the New Glenn Program. We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!

  

As part of the New Glenn SEIT system safety, reliability and risk team, you will work to develop processes and products for the design and evaluation of the New Glenn orbital launch vehicle system and facilities. You must have a passion for mission assurance, a commitment to the fundamentals of system safety/reliability, and a strong capacity to work collaboratively on complex and interesting new problems. jobs.title: Associate Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
**Associate Automation Engineer**
=================================

**Job Description**
-------------------

An Associate Automation Engineer is an entry-level engineering professional responsible for supporting the development, design, and implementation of industrial control systems for building automation projects. This role combines control system design, HMI/SCADA development, PLC/DDC programming, and field commissioning to ensure the successful delivery of projects under the guidance of senior engineers. An Associate Automation Engineer focuses on learning company standards, control system architecture, and software integration while contributing to project execution and system optimization.

**Education**
-------------

* Bachelor’s degree (preferred) or Associate degree in any of the following fields: Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Chemical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
* Trade school certificates or equivalent technical training combined with relevant experience may also be considered.

**Experience**
--------------

* 0–3+ years of experience in industrial automation, instrumentation and controls, PLC/DDC programming, or a related industrial engineering field.
* Familiarity with PLC/DDC and HMI configuration, industrial networking, and/or HVAC systems is preferred.
* Familiarity with construction site environments and field devices (instrumentation, valves, drives) is preferred.

**Skills**
----------

**Technical Skills:**

* Systems Knowledge: Basic understanding of HVAC and building automation systems (BAS).
* Control System Design: Ability to read electrical schematics, P&IDs, control system documentation, and network architecture drawings.
* HMI/SCADA: Basic experience with HMI and SCADA platforms (e.g., Rockwell, Ignition, Wonderware) and the ability to instantiate standard graphics, alarms, and trends.
* PLC/DDC: Basic understanding of PLC platforms (e.g. Allen-Bradley, Siemens) and at least one industrial automation programming language, such as Ladder Logic.
* Networking & Infrastructure: Basic understanding of industrial protocols (Modbus, BACnet, Ethernet/IP) and OT network design.
* Testing: Familiarity with troubleshooting techniques and tools such as simulators and multimeters for software testing and point-to-point device verification.

**Soft Skills:**

* Learning Mindset: A strong eagerness to learn new technologies and adapt to evolving engineering standards.
* Problem-Solving: A solution-oriented mindset with the ability to perform strategic debugging and know when to escalate issues.
* Attention to Detail: High commitment to accuracy in technical drawings, naming conventions, and project documentation.
* Communication: Ability to provide concise status updates and define technical challenges to project leads and team members.
* Leadership: Ability to collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary teams.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Control System Design: Perform product selection for common automation systems and applications and support generation of accurate control system drawings.
* HMI/SCADA Configuration: Instantiate graphics and configure HMI/SCADA screens in alignment with company standards.
* PLC/DDC Programming: Support basic PLC and DDC programming tasks such as tag configuration and control logic using standard templates, reusable code libraries, or custom code.
* Testing and Commissioning: Assist with testing, device verification, and troubleshooting during bench testing, Factory Acceptance Testing, and site startup activities. Travel may be required. Expect up to 30% travel, including regular overnight stays for non-local client sites and up to 100% travel to local client sites.
* Documentation: Maintain accurate project documentation, including IO lists, Sequence of Operations, Functional Specifications, test protocols, and redline markups.
* Safety & Compliance: Follow all office and site safety procedures and participate in mandatory safety training (e.g., OSHA-10).
* Quality Control: Ensure all document and code deliverables meet established quality standards for right-first-time accuracy and on-time delivery.

jobs.title: Controls Systems Engineer — Material Handling & Intralogistics
jobs.description:
**Step into a day where your code keeps freight moving**
--------------------------------------------------------

You start the morning scanning operational dashboards for anomalies across conveyors, sortation systems, scanners, vision systems, and print-and-apply equipment. A minor throughput dip pops on a line — you trace it to a PLC routine, adjust logic in RSLogix 5000 for an Allen‑Bradley ControlLogix rack, validate with the site team, and watch KPIs rebound. Before lunch, you review a contractor’s upgrade plan, ensuring licensed installations meet specs and safety codes. An after-hours alert comes in — you jump on remotely, triage the MHE controls software, and get the system back online fast. That’s impact you can measure in uptime, safety, and operational excellence.

**What you’ll own**
-------------------

* Champion a safe workplace by adhering to relevant codes, regulations, and company directives for system operations and work safety.
* Troubleshoot, modify, and optimize material handling control software for PLC/PC controllers, focusing on Allen‑Bradley ControlLogix/CompactLogix platforms and RSLogix 5000.
* Serve as the first‑line escalation for controls troubleshooting on‑site and remotely, during and after business hours; respond quickly to emergencies and coordinate assistance as needed.
* Inspect equipment to verify operation within design capabilities and client‑specified conditions.
* Scope, schedule, and oversee work performed by outside contractors, including proprietary work, licensed installs, upgrades, and inspections of specialized systems.
* Engineer process and reliability improvements from concept through network‑wide implementation.
* Monitor industrial networks (Ethernet, ControlNet, DeviceNet, Profibus, AS‑i) and powertrain systems (motor control, servo drives, VFDs) plus electrical distribution.
* Track MHE performance metrics and partner with site teams to eliminate electrical issues driving performance gaps.
* Communicate proactively with leadership, operations, and maintenance on technical issues, timelines, and production impacts; clearly convey complex topics and expectations.
* Lead failure reviews and process analyses; recommend improvements or retraining to prevent recurrence.
* Conduct control system assessments to sustain and elevate equipment reliability.
* Build strong relationships with the Client and the Operations Maintenance team; perform additional duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor’s degree preferred with 2–5 years of relevant experience; equivalent education/experience considered.
* Hands‑on exposure to at least two engineering design cycles (specification, component selection, programming).
* 2+ years working with PLC programming, robotics system components and controls, and SCADA‑based monitoring/control.
* Independent problem solver able to execute general instructions with minimal oversight.
* Schedule flexibility to support nights, weekends, holidays, and varied work areas; comfortable being on‑call on weekends as needed.
* Physical capability to stoop, stand, walk, climb stairs/ladders, and lift/carry 50 lbs+.
* Skilled at conveying sensitive and complex information, setting performance expectations, and resolving difficult issues.

**Preferred**
-------------

* 2+ years apprenticeship or equivalent experience in control systems troubleshooting/programming.
* Background supporting diverse conveyors and sortation systems.
* Experience with robotic maintenance.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.).
* Exceptional organization and a curious, investigative mindset.
* Advanced math skills, including percentages, fractions, and other financial‑related calculations.

**Tools & technologies**
------------------------

* PLC programming and SCADA experience
* Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC)

**Eligibility**
---------------

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future.
